Adaptive Wearable Biosensing Platforms for Diabetes Monitoring and Management

Abstract:

ContinuousGlucoseMonitoring(CGM)sensorsareimportantinthemanagementofdiabetes and other chronic non-communicable diseases due to their ability to assess glucose levels from interstitial fluid in a minimally invasive manner. However, their sensitivity may decline over time after implantation as a result of enzyme degradation and biofouling. Some CGM devices sometimes require daily manual calibrations to maintain the accuracy of the sensor sensitivity. Although calibration free sensors are available, sensitivity degradation still takes place which limits sensor lifetime without calibration. This work introduces a novel approach for predicting the variations in sensor sensitivity in vivo and automatically calibrating the sensor sensitivity by utilizing electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) for amperometric and potentiometric sensors. The surface of the sensor changes as a result of biofouling, which also leads to a reduction in sensitivity. The changes in impedance characteristics that occur due to the variations on the electrode were modelled using EIS and mathematical methods. In order to enhance sensitivity and sensor lifetime, the effect of highly porous gold (hpg) deposition on the electroless nickel immersion gold (ENIG) electrode was studied. The hpg coated electrode demonstrated better sensitivity and exhibited antifouling properties, hence prolonging sensor lifetime in comparison to other gold coating methods. Furthermore, a multi-analyte sensing platform was developed utilising a microneedle sensor array, demonstrating that a single platform can be utilised to detect multiple biomarkers. The sensor was functionalised to detect different analytes such as glucose, sodium, and potassium. The Mean Absolute Relative Difference (MARD) of this sensor obtained from animal studies was 7.20&plusmn2.00%. In order to reduce the chances of reducing sensor degradation due to biofouling and to increase sensor adoption, a wearable non-invasive sensor for multianalyte sensing was also developed. The sensor employed an external electric parallel field to extract glucose and potassium, enabling painless monitoring of these analytes. This platform was also validated through animal studies using Wistar rats. The Mean Absolute Relative Difference (MARD) of this sensor obtained from animal studies was 8.33&plusmn0.05%.
